The Signature presentation stresses why each principle holds, shows where it is used in real practice, and connects it forward to the Advanced material that follows.
core_concepts: Layering: full fuse melts flat, tack fuse keeps texture
Annealing: the slow cool that gives fused glass strength
key_laws: Never mix COE: incompatible glass cracks.
Program the full schedule including annealing; shortcuts shatter.
vocabulary: Full fuse: firing until layers melt completely smooth
Slump: firing glass over a mold to shape it
methods: Cut method: score in one firm pass, break over an edge or with running pliers, grind sharp edges
history: Kiln-formed glass is ancient; modern fusing grew with tested compatible glasses in the late 1900s, making home kiln work reliable.
